messages.author: fb92e83924bbcbf6
messages.subject: n.cluster with scantwo
parts:
Hello,

I'm running 1000 permutations with scantwo with the following line of
code on a computer with 16 GB of RAM (14 of which I have allocated to
running R).

pop11.sc2.perms <- scantwo(pop11, pheno.col=2, method="em",
n.perm=1000, model="normal", n.cluster=12)

But when I check the CPU usage using top, I see that each cluster is
using less than .5% of the computer CPU, and 77% is idle. Eventually,
the system crashes. When I used n.cluster with scanone, I had no such
problems. Also, when I calculate the genetic map, the CPU is fully
utilized. Any idea what the problem is?

Thank you very much,
Jen

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] n.cluster with scantwo
parts:
The jobs are probably running out of memory.
Try a smaller value of n.perm

karl

messages.author: fb92e83924bbcbf6
messages.subject: Re: n.cluster with scantwo
parts:
Thanks for the quick response -- I tried switching to just one perm,
but the process still did not go to completion (although at least the
computer didn't crash this time. It was just way too slow). Today I
have been trying to run the same line of code with one perm and one
chromosome, but I am still worried by the lack of CPU usage. My marker
set is very large -- the entire set has over 11,000 SNPs, the one
chromosome just 744. I'm using ten nodes this time, and again the %CPU
usage for each is around 0.4, with 97.6% of the computers cpu idle,
and it seems way too slow for just 744 markers and 1 perm. Do you know
what could be going on, or have any other ways that I might speed this
up? I don't actually care about identifying significant interactions
among my QTL, I just want to calculate a penalty so I can proceed with
model selection.

Thank you!
Jen

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] n.cluster with scantwo
parts:
I still think it's a memory problem; the lack of CPU usage likely indicates that there is "disk thrashing" (see http://tinyurl.com/3ffb98h).

If you are not interested in interactions, I would just get the 1d genome scan threshold (from permutations with scanone) and then in stepwise qtl use additive.only=TRUE and penalties=[the one threshold].

karl
